es: Distinguir obligación, prohibición, permiso y ausencia de obligación en normas escolares y vecinales (must, have to, be required to, must not, be permitted to, don't have to) y reconocer el marcador de cada una.

teaching.en: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.
teaching.es: Según el reglamento del colegio, todos los alumnos deben llevar el uniforme y cumplir con el código de vestimenta en todas las clases.
teaching.explanationEs: Be required to + verbo: obligación formal; el reglamento no dice «debes», sino «se exige». Comply with + norma: cumplirla.
segments: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the
uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.
teaching.audioText: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.

teaching.en: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.
teaching.es: La asistencia a la asamblea de la mañana es obligatoria, mientras que unirse al coro es totalmente opcional, así que nadie puede ser obligado a cantar.
teaching.explanationEs: Compulsory (y mandatory) son adjetivos de obligación propios de los reglamentos; optional marca lo que cada uno decide.
segments: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir
is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.
teaching.audioText: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.

teaching.en: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are permitted to use them at break in the yard.
teaching.es: Los teléfonos celulares están estrictamente prohibidos durante las clases, aunque los alumnos tienen permiso para usarlos en el recreo en el patio.
teaching.explanationEs: Are prohibited: prohibición formal, equivale a must not. Are permitted to + verbo: permiso formal, equivale a may o are allowed to.
segments: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are
permitted to use them at break in the yard.
teaching.audioText: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are permitted to use them at break in the yard.

teaching.en: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.
teaching.es: Los alumnos de bachillerato estarán exentos de la norma del uniforme, así que no tienen que llevarlo, pero llevarlo tampoco está prohibido.
teaching.explanationEs: Be exempt from + norma: quedar libre de una obligación. No tener que hacer algo (don't have to) no equivale a tenerlo prohibido (forbidden).
segments: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't
have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.
teaching.audioText: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.

teaching.en: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.
teaching.es: El personal no debe estacionar frente a la puerta, porque la obligación de mantener despejada la entrada se aplica a todos sin excepción.
teaching.explanationEs: Must not = prohibido. Ojo: no equivale a don't have to, que solo dice «no hace falta». Obligation es el sustantivo de lo que se debe hacer.
segments: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the
obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.
teaching.audioText: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.

teaching.en: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations leave the choice of project topic to each student.
teaching.es: Aunque el examen final es obligatorio para todos, el reglamento deja a cada alumno la elección del tema del proyecto.
teaching.explanationEs: Mandatory = obligatorio, sin excepción. Although + oración: contraste, no lleva but en la misma frase.
segments: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations
leave the choice of project topic to each student.
teaching.audioText: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations leave the choice of project topic to each student.

prompt.es: Según el aviso, ¿qué está prohibido?

choices.text: Locking a bicycle at the gate.
Riding a bicycle in the playground.
Cycling to school in the morning.

feedback.es: Are prohibited expresa una prohibición formal; permitted da permiso y optional deja la decisión libre.

origin.text: School notice: bicycles are prohibited in the playground, but pupils are permitted to lock them at the gate. Nobody is forced to cycle to school, because it is optional.

prompt.es: Completa: «La asistencia a la asamblea es obligatoria para todo el colegio.»

answer.text: compulsory
accepted: compulsory
mandatory
obligatory
required

feedback.es: Compulsory (o mandatory) califica una obligación que no admite excepción.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de obligación que aparece en los reglamentos.

origin.text: Every pupil has to be in the hall at nine. Attendance at the assembly is ___ for the whole school, and nobody can be excused without a note.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los visitantes no tienen permiso para entrar en la cocina.»

answer.text: Visitors are not permitted to enter the kitchen

feedback.es: Are not permitted to + verbo base es una prohibición formal; la negación va tras are.

hint.es: Empieza con Visitors; la negación va justo después de are.

prompt.es: Escucha a la directora y elige qué es obligatorio para los alumnos.

choices.text: Wearing a tie to every lesson of the school day.
Keeping their phones switched off for the whole break.
Signing in at the office when they arrive late.

feedback.es: Quien llega tarde debe firmar en la oficina: es obligatorio. La corbata es opcional y los celulares están permitidos en el recreo.

origin.audio: At the start of term, the head teacher read out the regulations. Every student is required to wear the uniform, she said, and arriving on time is compulsory: anyone who comes late must sign in at the office. Mobile phones are prohibited in class, although students are permitted to use them during break. Wearing a tie is optional, so nobody has to buy one, but running in the corridors is forbidden, for safety. She added that staff would comply with the same rules whenever they walked through the school with pupils.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la fuerza de la norma.

pairs: All pupils are required to wear a badge.
Bags are forbidden in the laboratory.
You may leave early on Fridays.
Year eleven will be exempt from assembly.

feedback.es: Required marca obligación, forbidden prohibición, may permiso y be exempt from una liberación de la obligación.

pairs: All pupils are required to wear a badge.
Bags are forbidden in the laboratory.
You may leave early on Fridays.
Year eleven will be exempt from assembly.

prompt.es: Lee el boletín: ¿qué postura refleja sobre la corbata?

choices.text: It accepts a small change while keeping the main rule.
It lowers its standards to cut costs for families.
It tightens the uniform rule after complaints from parents.

feedback.es: La corbata pasa a ser opcional, pero el uniforme sigue siendo obligatorio: un cambio pequeño que mantiene la norma principal.

origin.text: Dear parents, from September the uniform will remain compulsory, but the tie becomes optional. The school believes the change will reduce costs without lowering standards. Staff will check the uniform during the first week, and any student who is not in full uniform will be asked to comply by the next day.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué es obligatorio para los dueños de perros.

choices.text: Walking the dog on the grass near the playground.
Keeping the dog on a lead in the park.
Leaving the dog at home on weekend mornings.

feedback.es: Mandatory marca la obligación: el perro va con correa en el resto del parque. Pasear por la hierba es un permiso.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the meeting leader explained the new street rules. Dogs are forbidden in the playground, he said, but owners are permitted to walk them on the grass. Keeping a dog on a lead is mandatory in the rest of the park, and anyone who fails to comply with that rule may be fined. Cycling on the pavement is prohibited, although children under ten are exempt from it, since they are still learning to ride.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿con qué fin menciona el moderador la multa?

choices.text: To announce a new fine for cyclists on the pavement.
To ask owners to pay for damage.
To show that the lead rule will be taken seriously.

feedback.es: La multa se menciona como consecuencia de no cumplir la norma de la correa: subraya que se aplicará en serio.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the meeting leader explained the new street rules. Dogs are forbidden in the playground, he said, but owners are permitted to walk them on the grass. Keeping a dog on a lead is mandatory in the rest of the park, and anyone who fails to comply with that rule may be fined. Cycling on the pavement is prohibited, although children under ten are exempt from it, since they are still learning to ride.

prompt.es: Completa: «Todo el personal debe cumplir con el nuevo reglamento.»

answer.text: comply
accepted: comply

feedback.es: Comply with + norma significa cumplirla; se construye con with.

origin.text: The new regulations apply from Monday. All staff are required to ___ with them, or they may be fined.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es obligatorio llevar el uniforme en todas las clases.»

answer.text: Wearing the uniform is mandatory in every lesson

feedback.es: Mandatory es el adjetivo de obligación sin excepción; wearing el uniforme funciona como sujeto de la frase.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué quiere dejar claro la profesora sobre la norma de la piscina?

choices.text: That the rule protects young children rather than spoiling fun.
That older pupils may swim alone whenever they like.
That children under ten may swim only during lessons.

feedback.es: Dice que el objetivo no es estropear la diversión sino proteger a los más pequeños: la norma protege y no limita por limitar.

origin.audio: A sign at the pool says that children under ten may not swim without an adult, and a teacher explained the rule to a group of pupils. The aim is not to spoil anyone's fun, she said, but to keep the younger children safe. Older pupils are permitted to swim alone, provided that a lifeguard is here, and nobody is required to join the lesson if they have a note from home.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso: ¿qué se puede deducir?

choices.text: A jacket is compulsory, but the logo is left to each person.
A jacket is optional, but any jacket that staff wear must carry the logo.
A jacket is optional, and so is the logo on it.

feedback.es: El aviso no obliga a llevar chaqueta, pero impone una condición a quien la lleve: el logotipo.

origin.text: Notice to staff: wearing a name badge is required in all public areas. Staff are not forced to wear a jacket, but the regulations are clear that any jacket that staff wear at work must carry the company logo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Traer tu propio almuerzo es opcional, así que no tienes que traerlo.»

answer.text: optional
accepted: optional
voluntary

feedback.es: Optional describe lo que cada uno decide; don't have to confirma que traer el almuerzo no es obligatorio.

origin.text: The canteen is open every day. Bringing your own lunch is ___, so you don't have to bring one.

title.en: Shall, may not, is to be

es: Redactar normas en lenguaje reglamentario con shall, may not, is/are to be y must be / may be + participio, y reconocer su equivalente informal.

teaching.en: Borrowers shall return all loans within three weeks, in accordance with the terms printed on the back of the membership card.
teaching.es: Los usuarios devolverán todos los préstamos en un plazo de tres semanas, de acuerdo con las condiciones impresas en el reverso de la tarjeta de socio.
teaching.explanationEs: Shall en un reglamento = obligación formal («deberán»); no es el shall de ofrecimiento (Shall I help?). In accordance with + norma: conforme a ella.
segments: Borrowers shall return all loans within three weeks, in accordance with
the terms printed on the back of the membership card.
teaching.audioText: Borrowers shall return all loans within three weeks, in accordance with the terms printed on the back of the membership card.

teaching.en: Membership cards may not be lent to another person, and any card found on the premises without its owner will be handed to the desk.
teaching.es: Las tarjetas de socio no podrán prestarse a otra persona, y toda tarjeta hallada en las instalaciones sin su titular se entregará en el mostrador.
teaching.explanationEs: May not + be + participio: prohibición formal en pasiva; no se nombra a quien obedece. On the premises = dentro del local o edificio.
segments: Membership cards may not be lent to another person, and any card found
on the premises without its owner will be handed to the desk.
teaching.audioText: Membership cards may not be lent to another person, and any card found on the premises without its owner will be handed to the desk.

teaching.en: Overdue items are to be returned before the library closes, otherwise borrowers will be liable for a daily fine.
teaching.es: Los artículos con retraso se devolverán antes de que cierre la biblioteca; de lo contrario, los usuarios serán responsables de una multa diaria.
teaching.explanationEs: Is/are to be + participio: orden oficial e impersonal. Be liable for + multa o daño: tener que pagarlo.
segments: Overdue items are to be returned before the library closes,
otherwise borrowers will be liable for a daily fine.
teaching.audioText: Overdue items are to be returned before the library closes, otherwise borrowers will be liable for a daily fine.

teaching.en: Any damaged equipment must be reported to the front desk on the day the damage is noticed, and no attempt should be made to repair it at home.
teaching.es: Todo equipo dañado deberá comunicarse en el mostrador el mismo día en que se detecte el daño, y no se intentará repararlo en casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Must be + participio: obligación en pasiva; lo dañado es el sujeto. Report = comunicar, dar parte de algo.
segments: Any damaged equipment must be reported to the front desk on the day the
damage is noticed, and no attempt should be made to repair it at home.
teaching.audioText: Any damaged equipment must be reported to the front desk on the day the damage is noticed, and no attempt should be made to repair it at home.

teaching.en: Loans may be renewed once, provided that nobody has reserved the book, but renewal is not granted for items that are already overdue.
teaching.es: Los préstamos podrán renovarse una vez, siempre que nadie haya reservado el libro, pero no se concede la renovación de los artículos que ya están con retraso.
teaching.explanationEs: May be + participio: permiso formal en pasiva; provided that añade la condición. Renew = renovar.
segments: Loans may be renewed once, provided that nobody has reserved the book,
but renewal is not granted for items that are already overdue.
teaching.audioText: Loans may be renewed once, provided that nobody has reserved the book, but renewal is not granted for items that are already overdue.

teaching.en: Payment of fines is to be made at the desk within seven days, and borrowers shall not take out new loans while any item is overdue.
teaching.es: El pago de las multas se hará en el mostrador en un plazo de siete días, y los usuarios no podrán sacar nuevos préstamos mientras algún artículo esté con retraso.
teaching.explanationEs: Is to be made: orden oficial impersonal. Shall not + verbo base: prohibición formal («no podrán»). Take out a loan: sacar un préstamo.
segments: Payment of fines is to be made at the desk within seven days,
and borrowers shall not take out new loans while any item is overdue.
teaching.audioText: Payment of fines is to be made at the desk within seven days, and borrowers shall not take out new loans while any item is overdue.

prompt.es: Elige la versión formal de la primera norma del cartel.

choices.text: Borrowers will bring back the books in three weeks.
Borrowers can return books within three weeks.
Borrowers shall return books within three weeks.

feedback.es: Shall + verbo base es la fórmula reglamentaria de obligación; will y can no fijan una obligación.

hint.es: Busca el modal que usan los reglamentos para obligar.

origin.text: Informal notice on the library door: You must return books in three weeks. You can't lend your card to anyone. Tell us if a book is damaged.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los préstamos podrán renovarse una vez, salvo que el libro esté reservado.»

answer.text: may
accepted: may
can

feedback.es: May be + participio expresa el permiso formal en pasiva; unless añade la excepción.

hint.es: Es el modal formal de permiso, más reglamentario que can.

origin.text: Loans ___ be renewed once, unless the book has been reserved by another member.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los bolsos se dejarán en la entrada.»

answer.text: Bags are to be left at the entrance

feedback.es: Are to be + participio da una orden oficial sin nombrar a quien la cumple.

hint.es: Are to be + participio: orden impersonal.

prompt.es: Escucha el aviso y elige qué debe hacer quien quiera renovar un préstamo.

choices.text: Make sure nobody else has reserved the book.
Pay a small fine in advance at the desk.
Register again as a borrower at the desk.

feedback.es: La renovación se concede solo una vez y a condición de que nadie haya reservado el libro («provided that nobody has reserved»).

origin.audio: Good morning, and welcome to the library. A few words about how things work here. Borrowers shall return all loans within three weeks, in accordance with the terms printed on your membership card. Overdue items are to be returned at the desk, and borrowers will be liable for a small daily fine. Loans may be renewed once, provided that nobody has reserved the book. Damaged books must be reported to the staff, and no food or drink may be taken into the reading room on any account.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada norma formal con su función.

pairs: Borrowers shall register at the desk.
Food may not be eaten in the reading room.
Loans may be renewed once.
Overdue items are to be returned at once.

feedback.es: Shall obliga en activa, may not prohíbe, may be permite y are to be da una orden oficial.

pairs: Borrowers shall register at the desk.
Food may not be eaten in the reading room.
Loans may be renewed once.
Overdue items are to be returned at once.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso: ¿qué tono y propósito tiene?

choices.text: Informal and relaxed: it asks users to show cards if convenient.
Formal and firm: it sets an official rule with a consequence.
Angry: it warns users about heavy fines for any mistake.

feedback.es: Usa shall y anuncia una consecuencia para quien no cumpla: es una norma formal y firme, no una sugerencia.

origin.text: Library notice: from Monday, all users must show their membership card at the desk on request. Borrowers who do not do so shall be asked to leave the premises. This rule is introduced in accordance with the new safety regulations, and it applies to all users without exception.

prompt.es: Escucha a la bibliotecaria y elige qué no puede hacerse con los libros de consulta.

choices.text: Copying a few pages by hand.
Reading them inside the room.
Taking them out of the room.

feedback.es: «May not be taken out of the room» prohíbe sacar los libros de consulta; copiar páginas a mano sí se permite.

origin.audio: A librarian is explaining the rules to a new member. Reference books may not be taken out of the room, she says, although readers may copy a few pages by hand. Loans shall be limited to five items at a time, and overdue items are to be returned before any new loan is granted. If a book is damaged, the borrower should report it at once: nobody will be liable for damage that was reported honestly.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud adopta ella ante quien avisa de un daño?

choices.text: She is kind to users who report damage honestly.
She thinks reported damage should still lead to a fine.
She prefers that users quietly mend small damage themselves.

feedback.es: Dice que nadie será responsable de un daño comunicado con honestidad: es comprensiva con quien avisa.

origin.audio: A librarian is explaining the rules to a new member. Reference books may not be taken out of the room, she says, although readers may copy a few pages by hand. Loans shall be limited to five items at a time, and overdue items are to be returned before any new loan is granted. If a book is damaged, the borrower should report it at once: nobody will be liable for damage that was reported honestly.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los libros dañados deberán comunicarse al personal de inmediato.»

answer.text: reported
accepted: reported
communicated

feedback.es: Must be + participio forma la obligación en pasiva; reported es el participio de report.

origin.text: Please do not try to repair anything yourself. Damaged books must be ___ to the staff at once.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las multas se pagarán en el mostrador antes de las cinco.»

answer.text: Fines are to be paid at the desk before five

feedback.es: Are to be + participio da una orden oficial impersonal; before five fija el plazo.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué postura defiende la bibliotecaria sobre el lenguaje formal?

choices.text: That friendly wording is always better.
That formal wording gives rules more weight.
That the current notices already sound official enough.

feedback.es: Defiende que las fórmulas formales suenan a norma oficial y por eso la gente las toma en serio; su colega opina lo contrario.

origin.audio: At a committee meeting, the head librarian proposed changing the wording of the rules. Notices that say you must or you can't, she argued, sound like orders from a teacher, whereas borrowers shall and cards may not be lent sound like official rules, and people take them seriously. Her colleague disagreed: he thought that formal wording makes readers nervous, and he preferred a friendlier tone.

prompt.es: Lee la nota: ¿qué se deduce sobre los cobros por daños?

choices.text: They are charged automatically once a damage form is filled in.
They are the responsibility of the staff member.
They cannot be charged until the manager approves each case.

feedback.es: La nota dice que no se cobrará a nadie hasta que la dirección apruebe cada caso: el cobro depende de esa aprobación.

origin.text: To all staff: with effect from Monday, overdue notices are to be sent by email and not by post. Damaged items shall be recorded on the new form, and no borrower may be asked to pay anything until the manager has approved each case.

prompt.es: Escribe la norma formal sobre la tarjeta de socio.

answer.text: Users shall show their membership card to the staff.
accepted: Users shall show their membership card to the staff.
Users must show their membership card to the staff.
Membership cards are to be shown to the staff.
Membership cards must be shown to the staff.
Users are to show their membership cards to the staff.
Users shall show their membership cards to the staff.
Borrowers shall show their membership card to the staff.
Members shall show their membership cards to the staff.
Users shall show their membership card to staff.

feedback.es: Shall + verbo base (o la pasiva are to be shown) da la obligación formal que exige un reglamento.

origin.text: Escribe en inglés formal: los usuarios deberán mostrar su tarjeta de socio al personal.

es: Comprender un debate público: identificar quién decide, quién se beneficia y cuál es la razón de una norma, distinguir intención de impacto y reconocer lo que se encarga a terceros (have + objeto + participio).

teaching.en: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento decide las normas, pero los vecinos son quienes viven con ellas cada día, y rara vez tienen voz real en el resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: Quien decide y quien soporta la decisión son papeles distintos. Have a say: tener voz en una decisión.
segments: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with
them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.
teaching.audioText: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.

teaching.en: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and several of them have a vested interest, because the outcome will affect their income.
teaching.es: Comerciantes, padres y ciclistas son partes interesadas en el nuevo plan de tráfico, y varios tienen un interés personal, porque el resultado afectará a sus ingresos.
teaching.explanationEs: Stakeholder: quien se ve afectado por una decisión aunque no la tome. Vested interest: interés propio, a menudo económico.
segments: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and
several of them have a vested interest, because the outcome will affect their income.
teaching.audioText: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and several of them have a vested interest, because the outcome will affect their income.

teaching.en: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.
teaching.es: ¿Quién se beneficiará de la nueva norma y quién la pagará? Un buen debate siempre plantea ambas preguntas antes de votar.
teaching.explanationEs: Benefit from + norma: quien gana. Se contrasta con who pays, que señala a quien soporta el coste.
segments: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for
it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.
teaching.audioText: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.

teaching.en: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.
teaching.es: La razón de fondo es sencilla: menos autos significan calles más seguras cerca del colegio, aunque una norma que ayuda a unos puede ir a costa de otros.
teaching.explanationEs: Rationale: la razón que justifica la norma. At the expense of + personas o cosas: perjudicándolas para beneficiar a otros.
segments: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although
a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.
teaching.audioText: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.

teaching.en: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento sostiene que la prohibición pretende proteger a los niños, pero su impacto en los comercios podría ser serio; una consecuencia no prevista es un efecto que nadie había planeado.
teaching.explanationEs: Intended to = la intención; impact = el efecto real, que puede ser distinto. Unintended consequence: lo que pasa sin que nadie lo buscara.
segments: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact
on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.
teaching.audioText: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.

teaching.en: The council has the old bus shelter repaired by a contractor, which means it pays for the work but does not do it.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento hace reparar la vieja parada de autobús a un contratista, lo que significa que paga el trabajo pero no lo hace.
teaching.explanationEs: Have + objeto + participio: encargas el trabajo a otro; tú no lo haces. Contractor: empresa o persona contratada.
segments: The council has the old bus shelter repaired by a contractor, which
means it pays for the work but does not do it.
teaching.audioText: The council has the old bus shelter repaired by a contractor, which means it pays for the work but does not do it.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién toma la decisión.

choices.text: The council.
The residents.
The shop owners.

feedback.es: El verbo voted y el sujeto the council indican quién decide; vecinos y comerciantes solo hablaron en la reunión.

hint.es: El decisor es quien vota o aprueba la norma, no quien habla en la reunión.

origin.audio: The council voted last night to close Mill Street to cars during school hours. Residents and shop owners both spoke at the meeting, but only the council members took the vote.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿quién se beneficia de la norma?

choices.text: Shop owners, because they will sell more.
Parents, because the streets will be safer.
The council, because it will earn money.

feedback.es: Los padres ganan calles más seguras; los comerciantes temen un impacto negativo y el ayuntamiento habla de seguridad, no de beneficios.

prompt.es: Escribe tres normas para un parque comunitario con excepciones y una razón.

answer.text: Rule 1: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, in order to protect children and other animals, given that some dogs are not used to crowds. Rule 2: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, because the park is a quiet place for many families, and loud music is to be switched off at nine in the evening. Rule 3: Bicycles are to be left at the racks, apart from delivery bikes and children's bikes, so as to keep the main path clear for people on foot. The committee will review all three rules after six months, since a fair rule should change when the park changes. Anyone who disagrees may write to the committee, and please read these rules carefully before you enter.
accepted: Rule 1: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, in order to protect children and other animals, given that some dogs are not used to crowds. Rule 2: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, because the park is a quiet place for many families, and loud music is to be switched off at nine in the evening. Rule 3: Bicycles are to be left at the racks, apart from delivery bikes and children's bikes, so as to keep the main path clear for people on foot. The committee will review all three rules after six months, since a fair rule should change when the park changes. Anyone who disagrees may write to the committee, and please read these rules carefully before you enter.

First, rubbish must be taken home, except on festival days, because the bins are full by noon and the park looks dirty for the next visitors. Second, fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily and a single spark could close the whole park for a week. Third, dogs are to be kept on a lead, apart from guide dogs, in order to keep the playground safe for small children, who are often afraid of big animals. Finally, the gates shall be locked at ten unless the committee has approved an event, since neighbours need quiet at night. These rules are fair, because each one has a reason.

feedback.es: Una norma justa une una regla en pasiva, una excepción o condición razonable y una razón que la justifique (in order to, given that, since).

origin.audio: After the meeting, a member complained that the new rule had been announced too late. The chair agreed that the notice could have gone out earlier, but she pointed out that the rule takes effect only in May, which gives everyone time to prepare. She added that a notice that explains the reason is always better than one that simply gives an order. The member did not look convinced.
